text: Bryan Cantrill does a pretty good survey of caching strategies in the intro to this Papers We Love talk on the ARC in ZFS. [VIDEO]
Might I also recommend: Bryan Cantrill on ARC: A Self-Tuning, Low Overhead Replacement Cache [PWL SF] 10/2017 [VIDEO]

> it seemed natural to have a set of generations for items that have only been seen once, and then another generation for things that have been more active Have you looked at ARC? It sounds similar - it is a cache split between LRU and MFU areas, where the split point changes dynamically depending on the workload. [VIDEO] is a fun watch on the topic.

story: ZFS on Linux still has annoying issues with ARC size
text: The author calls ARC autotuning “opaque” which surprised me given a well regarded paper has been published on it: [LINK] [VIDEO] ...that said the author has been writing on the ARC for more than 10 years judging from his blog links so perhaps that paper did not answer his questions.
